notes:
Summary: enterprise evaluation focused on Dedicated capacity + SLA negotiation. Primary ask: clear alignment on latency SLO definition and measurement so legal + infra agree on credits and remediation. CTO: "We will not accept an SLA that measures only server-side 'generation' time — client experienced latency matters for product UX."

Key requirements (verbatim / paraphrase):
- Workload: multi-tenant customer support chat + reranking on search verticals. Short-turn interactive chats (avg 32-128 tokens). High QPS during peak windows (see throughput).
- Latency targets (initial ask from product): p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 700ms for non-streaming 1st-pass responses (64-token baseline). Streaming behavior: first-byte/initial-token latency must be comparable (p50 ~80ms) and per-chunk latencies <50ms to keep UI snappy.
- Measurement alignment: want explicit definitions — client-side end-to-end vs Redwood server-side vs network. Need SDK instrumentation guidance. Agreement: SLA will publish both server-measured generation times and an optional client-measured histogram for dispute resolution.
- Throughput / reserved GPU planning: estimate 1000 sustained RPS at baseline (64-token average) and burst to 5k RPS for 10-minute windows. Need to size reserved pool (GPUs and slots) and confirm model variants/quantization to hit p95 under load.
- Batching and concurrency: willing to accept some batching to reduce cost but must cap batch latency; need batching policy that targets tail SLOs.
- Observability: require per-request tracing id, token-level timings, per-model KPIs, and sample payload retention (30d) for debugging and QA.

Timeline / recent activities (bulleted):
- 2026-02-03: Intro call (Jordan / Priya) — overview of Redwood Dedicated and high-level SLA template (ff_2026-02-12_87431).
- 2026-02-12: Technical deep-dive — discussed p50/p95/p99 definitions and streaming vs non-streaming differences (Fireflies above). CTO insisted on client-side capture. Action: Redwood to propose measurement appendix.
- 2026-02-20: Infra readiness call — customer network team reviewed VPC peering checklist. Blocker: egress rules to allow telemetry.
- 2026-02-26: POC scoping — agreed to 2-week canary on dedicated small pool (4x A100 equiv) to validate p95 at 2k RPS. Payloads and prompt templates agreed.
- 2026-03-05: Cost/readout meeting — rough committed capacity numbers and ARR band reviewed with finance.
- 2026-03-08: Legal ask — request for explicit credit formula for latency breaches at p95 and p99 bands. Redwood to provide SLA appendix draft by 2026-03-12.

POC acceptance criteria (customer-defined):
- Sustained 2k RPS for 2 hours with p95 <= 300ms and p99 <= 900ms for baseline model and token length distribution.
- First-byte streaming latency p95 < 350ms.
- End-to-end sample traces from 1000 client sessions with SDK instrumentation showing correlation between client and server timers.
- Throughput per-GPU numbers and cost estimate validated within 20% of forecast.

SLA negotiation points to resolve:
- Exact measurement scope: server-only vs client-end-to-end vs hybrid (both reported, server-only used for billing credits unless large discrepancy).
- Tokenization and max-sequence assumptions for thresholds.
- Remedy tiers: credit percentages mapped to p95 and p99 breaches and number of breached minutes per month.
- Maintenance windows and exception handling for upgrades/rollouts.

Customer quotes / voice snippets:
- CTO: "If customers feel stutter on every chat turn we lose conversational utility — tail latency kills conversion."
- Product lead: "We need a deterministic plan for reserved capacity scaling during marketing spikes."
